title: One call answers where a symbol is defined, who uses it and what depends on a package, from the pinned map, without reading files
goal: kbingest.py where NAME [--map FILE|--repo REPO --rev REV] prints the definitions of NAME with path:line and pinned url, its references grouped by file, and for a package name the files and modules that import it, within a line budget, reading only the map; the kb MCP server serves the same as kb_code; a name the map lacks exits 1 naming the nearest names, never guessing; it works on a map of this repository and of an ingested one.

gates.question: When --repo has no cached map of the commit, what does where do?
options: build the map and cache it
refuse and name the map command
gates.recommendation: build the map and cache it
gates.reason: the one call answers a symbol question without a prior step, and a second call reads the cache
gates.answer: build the map and cache it

gates.question: How many body lines does where print by default, and what bounds --budget in kb_code?
options: 60 lines by default, kb_code takes 10 to 500
30 lines by default, kb_code takes 10 to 200
gates.recommendation: 60 lines by default, kb_code takes 10 to 500
gates.reason: one name with a few definitions and their reference files fits, and the part-share rule keeps the importers visible
gates.answer: 60 lines by default, kb_code takes 10 to 500

gates.question: Where is kb_code served, and is it read-only though a first call writes the map cache?
options: only the team's own server, readOnlyHint true
gates.recommendation: only the team's own server, readOnlyHint true
gates.reason: it reads a local repository and writes only a disposable cache under _cache/ingest/, as kb_backlog reads the clone
gates.answer: only the team's own server, readOnlyHint true

gates.question: What does where count as a name the map has, and what does it list for a missing one?
options: an exact definition name, a package name or an imported module (a prefix, or a relative import's last segment); nearest names by spelling, at most 5
gates.recommendation: an exact definition name, a package name or an imported module (a prefix, or a relative import's last segment); nearest names by spelling, at most 5
gates.reason: a package question has no definition, and a near miss lists names the map really holds
gates.answer: an exact definition name, a package name or an imported module (a prefix, or a relative import's last segment); nearest names by spelling, at most 5
